title: Decision Mistakes
objectives: Find unreachable branch mistakes (code that never runs)

hook.text: "IF grade ≥ 50 PASSED, ELSE IF grade < 50 FAILED": is that second check really needed, or is it redundant?

concept.heading: Uncovered case
concept.body: When an IF chain leaves some cases unhandled, that is an uncovered case mistake. For example, if you only check "grade ≥ 50" and "grade < 0", values between 0 and 50 (e.g. grade = 30) may not enter any branch. That is a logic error.

concept.heading: Unreachable branch
concept.body: In an IF chain, if an earlier condition always covers a later one, the later branch NEVER runs. For example, if "age ≥ 0" is checked first and something happens when it is TRUE, the check "age ≥ 18" after it can never be evaluated on its own (because the first condition has already "caught" it).

exercises.question: In the chain "IF grade ≥ 50 THEN Passed, ELSE IF grade < 0 THEN Invalid", what happens when grade = 30?
options: Nothing is written: an uncovered case

feedback.correct: Correct. 30 is neither ≥ 50 nor < 0, so no branch runs. This is an uncovered case mistake.
feedback.incorrect: 30 meets none of the conditions, so nothing is written. This is a case that was not handled (uncovered).

exercises.question: In the order "IF age ≥ 0 ... ELSE IF age ≥ 18 ...", why is the second condition (age ≥ 18) pointless?
options: It is not pointless at all
The first condition (age ≥ 0) is almost always TRUE, so the second branch is hardly ever entered
The second condition is always FALSE

feedback.correct: Correct. Since age ≥ 0 is TRUE for most real ages, the ELSE branch is almost never entered.
feedback.incorrect: The first condition (age ≥ 0) will always be TRUE for normal age values, so the second condition becomes practically unreachable.

exercises.question: What is the safest way to avoid an uncovered case mistake?
options: Add a "general" ELSE (a default case) at the end of the chain
Put the conditions in random order

feedback.correct: Correct. Adding a default ELSE at the end of the chain catches uncovered cases.
feedback.incorrect: Adding a catch-all ELSE block at the very end also handles the cases where no condition matches.

exercises.question: Complete the sentence.
exercises.template: When a range is left that no condition in an IF chain covers, that is an ___ case mistake.

exercises.question: What is the mistake in the order "IF score ≥ 90 ... ELSE IF score ≥ 95 ..."?
options: The order is reversed: the ≥95 check never runs, because ≥90 already catches it
Both conditions run at the same time

feedback.correct: Correct. The broader condition (≥90) is written first, so the narrower condition (≥95) is never tested. That is an unreachable branch.
feedback.incorrect: Since ≥90 already covers every case where the score is ≥95, the second check never runs on its own. It is an unreachable branch.

exercises.question: In nested threshold checks, what should the correct order usually be?
options: From the narrowest/highest threshold to the broadest/lowest threshold
From the broadest threshold to the narrowest threshold

feedback.correct: Correct. The highest/narrowest threshold must be checked first, otherwise a broad condition "catches" it and makes it unreachable.
feedback.incorrect: You usually start with the highest/narrowest threshold; otherwise a broad condition keeps the narrow one from ever being tested.

summary: Uncovered case: some value ranges meet no condition, so no branch runs.
Unreachable branch: an earlier broad condition keeps a later narrow condition from ever being tested.
Safe ordering: start from the narrowest/highest threshold and add a catch-all ELSE at the end.
